newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Feb 11.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Clashes between nomadic stock breeders and sedentary farmers in northern Ivory Coast hamper development in the region, particularly in the livestock sector, Ivorian official responsible for animal resources says.
- Construction work to extend and modernise Abidjan's Felix Houphouet-Boigny International Airport, well under way.

- German ambassador Hans-Albrecht Schraepler says in interview Germany is concerned about growing number of asylum seekers, most of them unjustified; says Ivorians welcome to train and study there on condition they return home afterwards.
- Eighth Panafrican Congress of Dermatology opens in Abidjan Thursday, under theme: "Tumors, Skin Pigmentation Disorders, STD/AIDS in Africa".
- Ivorian student federation FESCI calls a five-day strike in universities and institutions of higher education nationwide to press demands for release of detained student activists.

- Break-away Ivorian transport union forms; head of the National Union of Road Hauliers Groups of Ivory Coast (SNGT-CI) says there is room for it and the long-standing SYNTTCI union to operate in the sector.

- Commisssion investigating violence surrounding main opposition boycott of 1995 presidential election expected to report its findings in April; sources close to the ruling Democratic Party suggest it will find evidence on which to charge Ivorian Popular Front leader Laurent Gbagbo and Rally of the Republicans leader Djeny Kobina.
- Ministry of Family and Promotion of Women to organise a consultative meeting on February 22 on theme: "Participation of Women in the Development Process of the Ivory Coast".
